messages:
Maria: Heads up — seeing a coordinated rise in NVIDIA Xid 31 with intermittent Xid 13 from multiple hosts in eu-west-1 since ~08:10 UTC. Affected workloads: embedder + reranker. Putting triage notes here and tagging oncall.
monitoring-bot: alert: gpu_xid31.rate > 5/min (eu-west-1) hosts=[gpu-eu-23,gpu-eu-24,gpu-eu-47] severity=medium
Maria: @sre-oncall can you grab initial nvml dumps and kernel logs? I'm sampling a few embedder traces.
Adrian: on it. Any ECC counter trends or thermal spikes?
Maria: ECC counts flat; temps within normal. Logs show repeated kernel watchdog resets (Xid 31) and occasional Xid 13 kernel faults.
Ken: Pasting sample from gpu-eu-23 dmesg:
```
[2026-03-18T08:12:04Z] nvrm: Xid 31, GPU 0, process embedder-ctl pid=4219 seq=512
[2026-03-18T08:12:04Z] nvrm: GPU reset triggered
[2026-03-18T08:12:08Z] app: session reconnect
[2026-03-18T08:12:09Z] nvrm: Xid 13, kernel fault, stack truncated
```
Maria: thanks. Workload metadata: these embedder jobs are using batch=64, median seq_len ~1024, persistent KV caches hot.
Adrian: fits a long-kernel runtime pattern — Xid31 often from watchdog due to prolonged kernel execution. Could be int8 kernels + KV/cache causing long SM occupancy.
sre-oncall: launching a canary config on gpu-eu-24 with reduced batch (16) and fp16 fallback to see if kernel timeouts drop.
Jamie: reminder: fp16 fallback increases token cost ~15-25% depending on workload. Need to notify product owners if we flip traffic.
infra-bot: drain initiated on gpu-eu-23: `kubectl drain gpu-eu-23 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data` pods evicted: embedder-ctl-12, embedder-ctl-14
monitoring-bot: metric snapshot @08:20 UTC: Xid31 rate on gpu-eu-23 down 40% after drain; still elevated on gpu-eu-24,gpu-eu-47
Ken: checking gpu-eu-24 kernel logs — seeing Xid31 interleaved with PCIe AER messages. Snippet:
```
[08:15] nvrm: Xid 31, GPU 0
[08:15] pcieport 0000:65:00.0: AER: Uncorrected (Non-Fatal) error
[08:15] kernel: PCIe link retrained
```
Adrian: interesting. We did a rack firmware push last month in eu-west. Could be PCIe firmware/slot issues causing transient resets that cascade into the GPU driver watchdog. @infra-fw can you confirm firmware versions for these hosts?
Maria: pinging infra-fw OOO here but we can at least collect fw versions from sysfs and compare.
Jamie: operational question — if we mark these hosts degraded and shift embedder traffic cross-region, what are the perf/cost effects?
sre-oncall: eu-west embedder spare capacity ~12%. If we cold-migrate affected pods to us-west, expect median latency +30ms and cost +18% (egress + instance sizing). Short-term mitigation OK but not ideal for SLAs.
Ken: collecting per-GPU nvml counters, full dmesg, and 1h workload trace (batch sizes, seq_len distribution) for all affected hosts and uploading to /mnt/triage/eu-west/xid31-20260318.tar.gz — link in a minute.
Maria: immediate mitigation plan: 1) drain gpu-eu-23 (done) + driver module reload + host reboot scheduled 08:30 2) canary on gpu-eu-24 with batch=16 + fp16 3) request infra-fw to validate PCIe firmware and slot seating for gpu-eu-24/gpu-eu-47 4) notify product owners about temporary fp16 fallback and potential cost bump
sre-oncall: monitoring will keep Xid31/Xid13 rates under watch; if rates remain >1/min after these steps we'll schedule replacement for gpu-eu-24 (suspect flaky PCIe slot or riser).
Adrian: if the canary resolves Xid at lower batch sizes, that points to kernel timeouts from long-running kernels. If AER persists even after reboot, we should escalate hardware replacement.
Maria: action items assigned: Ken=collect logs + upload; sre-oncall=canary + monitor; infra-fw=firmware check; Jamie=notify product owners; Adrian=analyze kernel-time distributions. I'll update thread after 09:00 UTC. :thumbsup:
